note: The OLG has a dedicated TBA section (SNAP > Certification Types > TBA) with pages covering Overview, Case Maintenance, and Examples. It correctly covers several FNS 727 requirements: the 5-month transitional period, benefit recalculation by removing TAFDC income, household ineligibility criteria, no reporting requirements during TBA, and dual participation prevention (adjusting benefits when a TBA member joins another SNAP household). However, several FNS 727 elements are missing or incomplete: (1) The OLG only addresses TAFDC closures — there is no mention of SFCA (state-funded cash assistance) or EAEDC households with children, which FNS allows as an option. (2) The OLG does not explicitly document which household types receive TBA (all-TAFDC, mixed TAFDC/non-TAFDC, etc.) — it simply says 'certain TAFDC cases close due to income.' (3) The OLG does not explicitly state that benefits are 'frozen' at the recalculated amount throughout the transitional period, though the absence of reporting requirements and the BEACON automation imply this. (4) There is no documentation of whether Massachusetts opted to further adjust benefits based on changes learned from other programs during the TBA period. These gaps leave workers without a complete understanding of TBA's scope and the state's policy choices under FNS 727.
